title: Staying in California and putting a band together; Don Byas switched to tenor
summary: After a Cab Calloway tour west and a film with Al Jolson he stayed in California, assembled a band including Don Byas, whom he put on tenor and helped with mouthpieces.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: But anyway, we went to California. This is the first time, I think, Cab had gone to California. That's when I stayed out in California. But we went out there and played up and down the coast, in Frank Sebastian's Cotton Club, then we made a picture with Al Jolson, "The Singing Kid."
And then I stayed in California and Al Morgan came back to join me in California because I organized a band out there.

This is '36. And I had -- in fact Don Byas and Jack McVea and -- in fact, these fellows were all playing at Billy Papke's with a band named Charlie Echolls. So I went down and got all these guys together and they all joined my band. And Don Byas was an alto player and I put him on tenor. That's when he started -- he never did play alto again. I put him on tenor. And I used to sit with him and work with mouthpieces because when he first got the tenor
it was a little bit too much for him to play. And he became one of the giant tenor players of all times to my knowing, because he played with me again back in New York.
